newsitem.title: USA: Three big oil companies report higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: Three big oil companies report higher earnings.

text.p: Three big oil companies Monday reported a jump in earnings for the third quarter, boosted by strong production and higher oil and natural gas prices that more than offset weakness in refining operations.

The companies said average crude oil prices rose by as much as $4 a barrel in the quarter. While this boosted results in exploration and production, it raised costs for their refining and marketing businesses.
They also said chemical operations were hurt in the quarter by lower prices and higher raw material costs.

Texaco Inc. said net earnings jumped 50 percent, Chevron Corp. reported a 29 percent increase excluding special items and Exxon Corp., the nation's largest oil company, said profits rose 4 percent. The results were in line or slightly better than had been expected on Wall Street.
Mobil Corp., the No. 2 oil company, reported a drop in earnings, and Ashland Inc. reported a profit vs. a loss in the year-ago period.

Exxon, based in Irving, Tex., said net income for the quarter rose to $1.56 billion, or $1.25 a share, from $1.50 billion, or $1.20 a share, in the 1995 quarter. Sales rose almost 8 percent to $33.32 billion from $30.97 billion.
It said earnings from exploration and production jumped 65 percent as average crude oil prices rose $4.50 a barrel. Natural gas prices were also higher.
Earnings from refining and marketing fell from the year-ago period, reflecting tough competition and the rising cost of crude oil feedstocks.
Faifax, Va.-based Mobil said net earnings fell to $769 million, or $1.92 a share, from $786 million, or $1.95 a share, in the year-ago period. Sales grew to $20.3 billion from $18.6 billion.
Mobil cited tough market conditions, including strong crude prices that hurt refining and marketing results. It also noted its refineries were down more often than had been expected in the quarter.

"Since we are in a very competitive industry that has significant price volatility, changes in the way we run our business are essential if we are to compete in the long term," Chairman Lucio Noto said, but he did not elaborate.

Chevron, based in San Francisco, said net income jumped to $655 million, or $1 a share, from $282 million, or 44 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter, when one-time charges of $222 million depressed results. Excluding charges and a one-time gain of $5 million in the latest quarter, earnings rose 29 percent, it said.
Sales grew 18 percent to $11 billion from $9.3 billion.
Chevron said its average price for crude oil rose to $18.88 a barrel from $14.91 a barrel in the 1995 period. Average natural gas prices also rose sharply, to $2.06 from $1.40 for 1,000 cubic feet.

At Texaco, based in White Plains, N.Y., net income jumped to $434 million, or $1.61 a share, from $290 million, or $1.06 a share, for the 1995 quarter. Sales grew to $11.10 billion from $8.81 billion.
Its average price for crude oil rose $3.05 a barrel.

"Texaco's higher worldwide crude oil and natural gas production and the continuing strength in commodity prices led our strong third quarter and year-to-date results," Chairman Peter Bijur said in a statement.

Texaco stock jumped $2.125 to $105.50 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Analysts had been expecting per-share earnings of $1.46 on average, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.
Exxon stock rose 50 cents to $89.875, also on the NYSE. Analysts had forecast earnings of $1.21 a share, according to First Call.
Chevron added 50 cents to $67.875 on the NYSE. Analysts had been expecting earnings of 95 cents a share on average.

Ashland Inc., based in Ashland, Ky., said it earned $46 million, or 64 cents a share, in its fourth quarter, compared with a loss of $30 million, or 55 cents a share, in the 1995 quarter. Sales rose to $3.5 billion from $3.3 billion.
Ashland stock fell 25 cents to $42.625 on the Big Board. Analysts had forecast earnings of 66 cents a share.
